close_reason: False positive: bc.as_ref() is required because bc is consumed by bc.and_then() on the next line. Removing as_ref() causes a use-after-move compile error.
description: In chain_walk: 'bc.as_ref().map(|b| b.ca) != Some(true)'. bc is Option<BasicConstraints> (owned). Calling .as_ref() before .map() is unnecessary: .map() consumes the Option<T> and b.ca is Copy, so no borrow-lifetime concern. Should be 'bc.map(|b| b.ca) != Some(true)' or more idiomatically '!bc.is_some_and(|b| b.ca)'. The .as_ref() is noise that makes the reader double-check whether bc is being preserved.
title: bc.as_ref().map(|b| b.ca) should be bc.map(|b| b.ca) — as_ref is redundant on owned Option
